title: Activating the Annotator: Operationalising Lived Experience in Data Annotation
measurement_description: The paper measured the effect of an upstream, LLM-driven lived-experience elicitation procedure (AXLE) on human annotators' harm ratings, label entropy, and identity resonance when annotating ambiguous hate speech. Religion was one of three thematic scenarios used to evaluate whether activating an annotator's positionality changes their perception of harm and the rationales they cite.
findings: For ambiguous hate speech items in the religion domain, eliciting lived experience produced the largest uniform shifts in annotator judgments. Specifically, harm ratings increased significantly (from a mean of 2.53 to 3.33) and identity resonance increased sharply (from 2.89 to 3.47). Annotators moved together toward harsher readings of religion-focused items under elicitation without significantly increasing the dispersion (entropy) of the labels, contrasting with other domains where dispersion increased.
